selected_problem: Under-drainage during venous congestion — P_venous rises during Valsalva, sleep
mechanism_hypothesis: CLOSED-LOOP DRAINAGE CONTROL: continuously measure P_CSF and P_venous; adjust valve resistance (or drainage rate) to maintain target ICP despite variations in posture, respiration, venous congestion, and patient physiology.
key_insight: The eShunt's venous boundary is both the PROBLEM and the SOLUTION. P_venous variation causes over/under-drainage (problem), but P_venous is MEASURABLE, so the system can COMPENSATE (solution). VP shunts have the same over-drainage problem but cannot measure or compensate for peritoneal pressure.
eShunt_specificity: HIGH — the venous boundary is the load-bearing element. The closed-loop REQUIRES measuring P_venous, which is only possible in an endovascular CSF-to-venous shunt.

mechanism_families.mechanism: Active valve adjustment based on P_CSF - P_venous
mechanism_families.description: Micro-actuator adjusts valve opening pressure in real-time based on measured dP
mechanism_families.novelty_potential: HIGH — no existing shunt adjusts based on venous pressure
mechanism_families.engineering_complexity: HIGH — requires implantable micro-actuator + pressure sensors + control algorithm

mechanism_families.description: No moving valve; instead, variable-flow-resistance element (e.g., shape-memory alloy, electroactive polymer) adjusts drainage resistance based on measured pressures
mechanism_families.engineering_complexity: MEDIUM — no mechanical valve, solid-state resistance change

mechanism_families.description: Multiple drainage paths with different resistances; system selects path based on current pressure state
mechanism_families.novelty_potential: MEDIUM — multi-stage valves exist but not pressure-adaptive

mechanism_families.description: System learns patient's typical P_CSF/P_venous patterns and PREDICTS needed drainage adjustment (e.g., before patient stands up, pre-adjust valve)
mechanism_families.novelty_potential: VERY HIGH — predictive drainage control is novel
mechanism_families.engineering_complexity: HIGH — requires implanted processor + learning algorithm
mechanism_families.connection_to_position_1: This mechanism uses the hydraulic state estimation from Position #1 (active interrogation) to PREDICT and PRE-ADJUST drainage. This is a PLATFORM connection.

mechanism_families.description: Not fully active — a passive valve whose threshold automatically compensates for P_venous changes (e.g., reference chamber connected to venous pressure)
mechanism_families.novelty_potential: MEDIUM-HIGH — venous-compensated passive valve is novel
mechanism_families.engineering_complexity: LOW — no electronics, purely mechanical compensation
mechanism_families.advantage: Simplest to manufacture and regulate; no battery needed; closest to CereVasc's existing passive valve

recommended_approach: Start with mechanism 5 (venous-pressure-compensated passive valve) as the simplest testable hypothesis, then explore mechanism 4 (predictive closed-loop) as the higher-value platform play. Mechanism 5 is the 'minimum viable invention'; mechanism 4 is the 'platform invention'.
